prompt:
Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

Every category has a bidirectional nature. For example:

One person's sensitivity to the Care/Harm foundation may lead them to support high levels of immigration from poorer nations, to reduce the suffering of those who migrate. Whereas another person's sensitivity to the very same foundation may lead them to oppose those levels, because they believe it could lead to people they care about being harmed.

TEXT_E:
Conservative Party Manifesto 2019 – Summary

Core guarantee and choice: With a Conservative majority, we will pass our oven‑ready Brexit deal immediately, leave the EU in January, and unleash the potential of the whole UK. We will deliver: more funding for the NHS (50,000 more nurses, 50 million more GP appointments), 20,000 extra police and tougher sentencing, an Australian‑style points‑based immigration system, massive investment in science, skills, schools and infrastructure within strict fiscal rules, Net Zero by 2050, and no rises in the rates of income tax, VAT or National Insurance. The alternative is a Corbyn/SNP coalition with two divisive referendums and more chaos.

Get Brexit done: End paralysis and restore certainty. Leave the customs union and single market; no political alignment or ECJ jurisdiction. Take back control of laws, borders, money and trade policy; agree a friendly UK‑EU FTA in 2020 without extending implementation. Use new freedoms for freeports, animal welfare reforms and VAT cuts (e.g., abolish the tampon tax).

Unleash Britain’s potential: Because Conservatives fixed Labour’s mess and restored the public finances, we can now invest responsibly. We will not borrow for day‑to‑day spending; debt will fall over the Parliament. We back superb public services because they are the bedrock of a dynamic, free‑market economy.

NHS and social care: Record cash boost, 40 new hospitals and 20 upgrades, 6,000 more GPs and 6,000 more primary care professionals, an NHS Visa, faster access to cutting‑edge medicines, mental health at parity, better screening, and free parking for those most in need. Cross‑party reform of social care with £1bn extra every year and a guarantee no one will have to sell their home to pay for care; more support for carers and doubling dementia research.

Education and skills: £14bn extra for schools, per‑pupil funding guarantees, teacher starting pay at £30,000, firm discipline backed by Ofsted, an arts premium, sport, SEND support, and more great free schools. A £3bn National Skills Fund, upgraded FE, Institutes of Technology, more apprenticeships tied to major projects, and a UK Shared Prosperity Fund to level up skills.

Safer streets and justice: 20,000 more police, fair and proportionate stop and search, tougher sentences (ending automatic halfway release for serious crimes; whole‑life for child murderers), more prison places, a new cyber force, crackdowns on knives, drugs and online harms, a Victims’ Law and stronger action on domestic abuse.

Controlled, fair immigration: A points‑based system that prioritises skills and contribution, treats EU and non‑EU equally, reduces lower‑skilled migration and overall numbers, fast‑tracks NHS staff and top talent, increases the NHS surcharge, requires contribution before benefits, and learns from Windrush.

Levelling up, housing and infrastructure: A £100bn infrastructure revolution—Northern Powerhouse Rail, Midlands Rail Hub, strategic roads, an EV rapid‑charge network, bus reform, cycling, Beeching reversals, and nationwide gigabit broadband by 2025. A Towns Fund, safer streets, cultural investment and English devolution. Build at least a million homes this Parliament, encourage long‑term fixed‑rate mortgages, discount homes for locals/key workers, end no‑fault evictions, reform leasehold, renew Affordable Homes, end rough sleeping, and protect the Green Belt.

Business, innovation and tax: Keep taxes low and predictable; raise the NI threshold; lift the National Living Wage to two‑thirds of median pay by 2024. Cut and reform business rates, tackle late payments, expand start‑up loans, boost R&D tax credits to 13%, support self‑employed, strengthen anti‑avoidance, and back high‑risk/high‑reward science. Free trade ambition with 80% of trade under FTAs in three years—USA, Australia, New Zealand, Japan—while protecting standards. The NHS is not on the table.

Environment and rural/coastal Britain: Lead the world to Net Zero by 2050 with market‑led clean growth—40GW offshore wind by 2030, CCS, hydrogen and nuclear, £9.2bn for energy efficiency, clean transport, and a moratorium on fracking unless proven safe. An Environment Bill with an independent watchdog, major tree planting, peatland restoration, anti‑plastic measures, and strong animal welfare.

Strengthen the Union and Britain in the world: Oppose a second Scottish referendum; level up every nation with the UK Shared Prosperity Fund and freeports. Maintain defence spending above 2% of GDP, modernise our Armed Forces, keep Trident, create Space Command, support veterans, uphold 0.7% aid, use Magnitsky sanctions, and champion media freedom and girls’ education.

Renew our democracy: Restore trust—voter ID, fair boundaries, protect free speech and a free press, maintain First Past the Post, and establish a Constitution, Democracy & Rights Commission to ensure effective, accountable government.

Only a Conservative majority will get Brexit done and take our one‑nation, low‑tax, high‑wage, green and secure United Kingdom forward.

TEXT_D:
Liberal Democrats 2019 Manifesto – Summary (ideological framing preserved)

Core values: Build and safeguard a fair, free and open society. Disperse power, protect liberty, equality and community, champion human dignity, creativity and diversity. Government’s role is to enable people to thrive and take part in decisions affecting their lives.

Stop Brexit, choose openness: The Lib Dems are the unapologetic party of Remain. A Lib Dem majority would revoke Article 50; otherwise they will back a People’s Vote with the option to stay. Remaining delivers a £50bn “Remain Bonus” to invest in schools and tackling inequality, protects jobs, the NHS, science, peace in Northern Ireland, UK unity and freedom of movement.

A stronger, fairer, innovation-led economy:
- £130bn for climate-friendly infrastructure: transport, energy, schools, hospitals and 300,000 homes a year (100,000 social).
- UK2050: lift R&D to 3% of GDP; expand Catapults; spread innovation beyond the South East; ethical tech via a Lovelace Code; citizen benefit from data; support creative industries.
- Skills Wallets: £10,000 for every adult for lifelong learning; expand high-quality apprenticeships; a Skills & Training Levy.
- Wellbeing Budget: judge policy by wellbeing as well as GDP.
- Fair taxes: restore Corporation Tax to 20%; replace Business Rates with a land value-based Commercial Landowner Levy; stronger action on multinational tax avoidance and tech giants.

Future of work and responsible business:
- New “dependent contractor” status with basic rights; flexible working from day one; higher minimum wage premium for zero-hours; union access; enforce prompt payment; employee voice on boards; duty of care on environment and human rights in supply chains.

Climate emergency and nature:
- Net zero by 2045; 80% of electricity from renewables by 2030; ban fracking; £12bn for clean power.
- Insulate homes by 2030; zero‑carbon new homes by 2021 (rising to Passivhaus by 2025); end fuel poverty by 2025.
- Clean transport: EV-only new cars/vans by 2030; rail network ultra‑low‑emission by 2035; fares freeze; more buses, trams, cycling; Clean Air Act.
- Nature Act with binding targets; 60m trees/year; peatland and wetland restoration; 50% UK waters protected; circular economy and zero‑waste laws (deposit returns, right to repair).

Education and childcare:
- Free, high‑quality childcare: 35 hours/week, 48 weeks/year from 9 months for working parents; triple Early Years Pupil Premium; £1bn for Children’s Centres.
- Reverse school cuts; hire 20,000 teachers; fix SEND funding; scrap SATs and league tables; replace Ofsted; protect arts; “curriculum for life.”
- FE uplift; restore maintenance grants; Student Mental Health Charter.

Health, mental health and care:
- 1p on Income Tax (raising £7bn/year) ringfenced for NHS and social care; £10bn capital; integrate services; end automatic tendering.
- Mental health parity: new waiting time standards, 24/7 crisis care, perinatal support; free prescriptions for chronic MH conditions; implement Mental Health Act reforms.
- Support carers with respite, higher earnings threshold; ethical international recruitment; more GPs and multidisciplinary teams.
- Public health first: Wellbeing Strategy; Clean Air right; obesity and alcohol harm reduction; regulate cannabis via a legal, licensed market; decriminalise abortion UK‑wide; PrEP access.

A fair society: dignity, security, homes
- Fix Universal Credit: first payment in 5 days; scrap two‑child limit and benefit cap; right to food; raise Local Housing Allowance; abolish bedroom tax; humane disability assessments.
- Housing: build 300,000 homes/year incl. 100,000 social; zero‑carbon standards; Rent‑to‑Own; 3‑year tenancies; tackle second homes; end rough sleeping in 5 years.
- Rural/coastal: buses, broadband, local hubs.

Safe communities, smart justice:
- Public health approach to violence; restore community policing; invest in youth services; Online Crime Agency; end disproportionate stop and search.
- Reduce reoffending: presumption against short sentences; more rehabilitation; women’s justice reform.

Rights, equality, and humane migration:
- Defend the Human Rights Act/ECHR; curb mass surveillance and police facial recognition; expand equality protections (GRA reform, X passports, BSL Act, end period and “pink” taxes).
- Scrap the hostile environment; 28‑day detention limit; right to work after 3 months; fair visas; welcome refugees (including 10,000 unaccompanied children over 10 years).

Better politics and devolved power:
- Proportional representation (STV), votes at 16, EU citizens’ votes, Lords reform; citizens’ assemblies; party‑funding transparency.
- A federal UK, stronger devolution and local fiscal powers.

A better world:
- Lead with allies through the EU, UN, NATO; keep 0.7% aid; Magnitsky‑style sanctions; suspend arms to Saudi; recognise Palestine; protect Hong Kong BNOs; cyber‑defence; maintain a minimum nuclear deterrent while pursuing multilateral disarmament; global climate leadership.

Judge whether TEXT_E or TEXT_D aligns more closely with this profile, taking into account that each foundation may be invoked in either direction.

Respond with a single JSON object and nothing else. Do not wrap it in markdown code fences and do not add commentary before or after it. The object must have exactly these keys, in this order:

{
  "evidence": "<the specific commitments in each text you relied on>",
  "reasoning": "<two sentences connecting that evidence to the verdict>",
  "confidence": "high" | "medium" | "low",
  "winner": "TEXT_E" | "TEXT_D"
}
